result:
I fixed the root cause in `src/lib/event-bus.ts`, and the edit is complete. I did not run the test suite, since this is a fix task and I didn't install or execute anything.

The bug: `subscribe()` copied the handler set on every call and stored the copy. The unsubscribe function deleted from the copy it had captured, which stops being the live set as soon as another subscribe happens. After a detach and re-attach cycle, the old handlers were never really removed, so each cycle stacked another copy. That explains the duplicate webhooks, audit rows and usage increments.

The fix keeps one live `Set` per event type. The unsubscribe now deletes from the current set for that type. Re-subscribing the same handler reference is still a no-op, because `Set` dedupes it. `emit()` already snapshots the set before iterating, so changes made during delivery are safe.

In-app notifications are unaffected. `notification-service.ts` attaches its handlers once at module load behind a `registered` flag and never detaches them, so they were never part of the detach/re-attach cycle.
